pages.title: Journeys and Regional Advice
pages.content:
Journeys

Journeys and Regional Advice

Travel health requirements depend on the specific route, lodging, and timing of your departure. We design immunisation plans matched to the geographic realities of where you will travel.

Safari and rural East Africa

Travel through Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, or Uganda often involves moving between urban hubs, rural safari reserves, and overland border crossings. During your consultation, we review yellow fever requirements and whether your route mandates the official International Certificate of Vaccination for border entry. We evaluate risk profiles for hepatitis A and typhoid, especially for travellers visiting rural communities or tented camps. Timing is critical for these destinations: yellow fever vaccines require at least ten days to establish legal border validity. We recommend visiting six weeks before flying to ensure your protective schedule is fully completed.

Plan this journey

Backpacking Southeast Asia

Extended journeys through Vietnam, Thailand, Cambodia, or Indonesia feature flexible routes, homestays, and extensive street food exploration. For these open itineraries, protection against food and waterborne infections is paramount. We routinely discuss injectable typhoid and hepatitis A immunisation to safeguard basic digestion. Furthermore, we evaluate whether extended rural stays, monsoon travel, or agricultural excursions warrant a discussion regarding Japanese encephalitis. Because backpackers frequently modify plans mid-trip, we prepare you with clear guidance on food safety, water treatment, and insect precautions that remain practical wherever your route leads.

Plan this journey

The Andes and the Amazon

Journeys combining mountain highlands and tropical lowlands, such as travel from Lima and Cusco into the Amazon basin, present paired environmental challenges. Rapid ascents into high mountain elevations require careful discussion of gradual acclimatisation and altitude illness prevention. Meanwhile, descending into rainforest river basins introduces potential exposure to yellow fever, requiring proof of vaccination for local transit or regional border posts. We also evaluate rabies pre-exposure immunisation for trekkers spending days away from immediate medical support. Our clinicians ensure your plan addresses both high-altitude physiology and lowland infectious risks.

Plan this journey

Long stays: study, work, volunteering

Living overseas for a semester, employment posting, or humanitarian project places you in prolonged contact with local communities and varied healthcare environments. We review your complete immunisation history to ensure routine childhood vaccines and boosters are current. Long-term placements often require rabies pre-exposure series, hepatitis A completion, and specific documentation for institutional visas. Our team provides formal medical summary letters and certified records that satisfy university admissions and corporate occupational requirements. We advise arranging your appointment six weeks in advance to allow multi-dose schedules to finish before your departure.

Plan this journey

Method

Every plan is decided at the visit.

These notes are where the conversation starts.

Families

Travelling with children

Family travel requires a thoughtful, reassuring approach. At Tabiji Clinic, nurse Priya Raman RN oversees paediatric consultations, coordinating travel doses with provincial childhood immunisation schedules. Children have distinct metabolic rates and dosing guidelines, meaning each recommendation is carefully calibrated to the child's age, weight, and previous vaccinations. We maintain a calm clinic atmosphere where children can ask questions and feel comfortable throughout their visit. Every family plan is decided collaboratively during your consultation; these regional notes are simply where our conversation starts.

pages.title: Your Appointment
pages.content:
Your appointment

Your Appointment

We structure every initial consultation around a full sixty minutes to ensure thorough clinical care. Our appointments follow an unhurried three-part sequence designed for your safety.

01 | Review

Twenty minutes across the desk

Your appointment begins with an in-depth twenty-minute conversation across the desk. Rather than relying on generic destination lists, your clinician sits with you to trace your actual itinerary on a map. We examine the specific cities, rural villages, elevation shifts, and accommodations you will encounter. We also review your complete immunisation history, current prescription medications, allergies, and prior travel experiences. This careful review identifies true risks while eliminating unnecessary vaccines, resulting in a transparent, personalised travel-health plan tailored to your health and journey.

02 | Doses

Twenty-five minutes, with a rest

Once you have approved your recommended immunisation plan and its pricing, we proceed to vaccine administration. Our travel-health nurses prepare each dose directly from monitored medical refrigeration units using gentle, practiced injection techniques. This twenty-five-minute block includes a fifteen-minute rest period in our clinic lounge following the injections. Resting allows us to monitor you closely for any immediate sensitivities, vasovagal responses, or questions. This observation window is an essential clinical standard at Tabiji Clinic to support your comfort and well-being before you depart.

03 | Record

Fifteen minutes, one stamped record

The final fifteen minutes of your hour are dedicated to comprehensive documentation. We record exact vaccine names, batch numbers, dosage volumes, and administration sites in your medical file. We complete your physical International Certificate of Vaccination or personal immunisation booklet, affixing required clinical stamps and clinician signatures. We provide clear written instructions detailing what to expect after vaccination, along with scheduling any required booster visits. You leave our clinic with official, border-ready records that border authorities and overseas institutions recognise without hesitation.

What to bring to your visit

To make the most of your sixty-minute consultation, please bring several key items to your appointment.

  • First, bring your detailed travel itinerary, including flight dates, internal transport plans, and names of lodgings or rural tour operators.
  • Second, gather any previous immunisation records, yellow vaccination cards, or childhood health booklets you possess.
  • Third, compile an up-to-date list of your current prescription medications, over-the-counter supplements, and known allergies.
  • Finally, bring your current passport number, which is legally required to issue an official International Certificate of Vaccination for yellow fever.

pages.title: Vaccines and Fees
pages.content:
Fees

Vaccines and Fees

We believe travel healthcare pricing should be transparent and established before any clinical care begins. All services and immunisations are billed in Canadian dollars.

Fee schedule

Consultation and vaccine fee schedule

We confirm your plan and its total before any dose is given.

Group clinics for eight or more people are quoted per group.

What a consultation includes

A consultation at Tabiji Clinic is a comprehensive sixty-minute clinical assessment conducted by an experienced travel-health professional. Your clinician evaluates your detailed itinerary, lodging standards, planned outdoor activities, and underlying medical history. We review mandatory border regulations, regional disease transmission cycles, and relevant travel advisories. You receive an individualised, written immunisation plan with clear rationale for each recommendation. We discuss mosquito prevention, water purification, altitude acclimatisation, and travellers' diarrhea self-treatment. We discuss and agree on every proposed dose and its exact fee before administering any vaccine.

Book a consultation

Paying and receipts

Payment is settled at the conclusion of your visit at our front desk. We provide clear, itemised medical receipts specifying the consultation fee, individual vaccine names, DIN numbers, and batch details. While travel consultations and preventive vaccines are not covered by provincial health plans, many extended workplace health benefits and private travel insurance plans offer partial or full reimbursement. Our administrative team, led by Mei-Lin Chou, ensures your receipt includes all required clinical identifiers so you can submit your claim directly to your third-party insurance provider without delay.

Records and receipts

Cold chain

Vaccine storage and cold chain management

Maintaining vaccine stability demands strict temperature control at every stage of handling. Our dispensary refrigerators are monitored continuously by our pharmacist, Samuel Achterberg. We utilize calibrated medical-grade cold storage systems with automated temperature logging that keep biologicals within precise clinical thresholds. Daily visual inspections, battery-backed temperature alarms, and documented lot verification protect the integrity of our inventory. This rigorous cold chain protocol protects the quality and proper storage condition of every vial administered in our clinic.

pages.title: Records and Certificates
pages.content:
Records

Records and Certificates

We issue official travel documentation that meets international health regulations and border requirements worldwide. Your physical record travels with you to every crossing.

Your record

Your record travels with you

Border officials, immigration officers, and overseas institutions require physical, verifiable proof of your immunisation history. A handwritten scrap of paper or an unverified digital note can cause delays or refusal of entry at international border checkpoints. At Tabiji Clinic, we document every dose in a durable physical format designed to withstand years of travel. Every entry includes the international nonproprietary name of the vaccine, the date of administration, the manufacturer lot number, and the official clinic stamp with clinician signature.

Certificates

Yellow fever certificates and international border entry

Yellow fever vaccine administration requires an official International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis, commonly known as the yellow card. This document is legally required for entry into specific nations in sub-Saharan Africa and tropical South America, as well as for travellers arriving from endemic regions. The certificate becomes legally valid ten days after the primary injection and remains valid for the traveller's lifetime under current World Health Organization regulations. To ensure border acceptance, your certificate must bear our designated yellow fever clinic stamp, the supervising clinician's signature, and your exact passport number.

Yellow fever certificate

Record summary for school or work

Lost booklet re-issue

Record summary for school or work

Universities, volunteer agencies, and multinational employers often mandate detailed proof of immunisation before approving international placements. We prepare formal record summaries that transcribe your lifetime vaccinations into standardized, institutionally acceptable reports. Supervised by Mei-Lin Chou at our records desk, our team reviews your historical immunisation documents, verifies administered doses against institutional compliance forms, and prepares an official medical summary letter. These certified summaries streamline academic registration, work permit processing, and visa applications for long-term overseas stays.

Ask for a summary

Lost booklet re-issue and historical file review

If you have misplaced your international vaccination booklet, we can reconstruct and re-issue your documentation. For a fee of CA$40, our records team conducts a thorough review of your clinic records and verified prior records, transcribing your confirmed vaccine history into a replacement booklet. This service includes a signed summary letter detailing your verified immunisation dates, vaccine lot numbers, and clinic registration. Having an intact, up-to-date replacement booklet ensures that future travel plans and border crossings proceed smoothly without the need to repeat valid vaccine courses.

pages.title: Groups and Schools
pages.content:
Groups

Groups and Schools

We organize structured travel-health clinics for organizations, academic institutions, and corporate teams deploying abroad. We prepare your entire delegation with coordinated care.

For teams

A clinic that comes to your team

Managing travel healthcare for a team or student group requires structured coordination. At Tabiji Clinic, our group services are directed by Tomás Varga, who works closely with organizational leaders to streamline pre-travel preparations. Whether you are sending a dozen engineers on a field project or thirty students on a semester abroad, we coordinate risk assessments, vaccine scheduling, and medical records. Group sessions ensure that every team member receives consistent health education, appropriate immunisations, and identical documentation before departure.

Occupational travel health for employers

Corporate employers, engineering firms, non-governmental organizations, and media crews regularly deploy personnel into regions with specific infectious disease risks. We offer customized workplace clinics that minimize employee downtime while maintaining duty of care standards. Depending on your operational requirements, clinics can be hosted at our Gastown practice or conducted on-site at your facility. We manage individual health clearances, administer necessary vaccines such as typhoid, hepatitis A, and yellow fever, and supply consolidated administrative documentation for corporate travel compliance.

Ask about a team clinic

Schools and universities

Secondary schools, universities, and research institutes organizing overseas field schools, study abroad programs, or athletic tours require rigorous health oversight. We collaborate with faculty advisors and group coordinators to review destination itineraries and participant medical requirements. Our clinical team delivers comprehensive briefings covering regional infectious risks, food safety, water purification, and vector avoidance. We complete all required institutional immunisation forms and issue official vaccination booklets, giving students, parents, and academic administrators peace of mind.

Ask about a school clinic

Booking requirements and group clinic logistics

Group clinics require a minimum threshold of eight individuals. Because multi-dose vaccination series and cold chain logistical preparations require advance planning, we recommend contacting Tomás Varga six weeks prior to your intended departure date. Pricing for group clinics is quoted per group, based on participant numbers, destination risk factors, and location requirements. We ensure all vaccine stock is reserved and cold-chain verified by our pharmacist in advance, allowing your group's appointments to run smoothly and efficiently.

pages.title: Our Team
pages.content:
Team

Our Team

Our clinical team brings together experienced travel-health physicians, specialized nurses, pharmacy staff, and administrative coordinators. We work collaboratively to deliver thorough, personalized care.

Seven people

One practice, one hallway.

Clinical direction and physicians

Her work across varied geographic terrains established our clinic's focus on itinerary-based pre-travel assessment. Dr. Mateo Ruiz is a physician specialising in altitude medicine and expedition travel, guiding travellers heading to high mountain ranges, trekking circuits, and remote environments. Together, our physicians establish all clinical protocols, evaluate complex medical histories, and oversee our yellow fever designation.

Priya works closely with parents to design manageable dosing timelines for younger travellers, ensuring visits are reassuring and unhurried for children of all ages.

pages.title: Frequently Asked Questions
pages.content:
FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

Here are answers to common questions about appointment timing, vaccine requirements, and travel health documentation. We encourage you to reach out if you have specific concerns.

How early should I book?

We recommend booking your travel consultation six weeks before your scheduled departure.

Read the answer

Can I come the week before I fly?

Yes, booking an appointment the week before departure is still very much worth your visit.

Read the answer

Do children need a different plan?

Yes, paediatric travellers require carefully tailored travel health plans.

Read the answer

What if I lose my booklet?

If you misplace your official vaccination booklet, we can re-issue your records.

Read the answer

All questions

Everything we are asked most

How early should I book?

We recommend booking your travel consultation six weeks before your scheduled departure. Certain immunisations require multiple doses spaced over several weeks to confer full protective immunity, such as hepatitis series or rabies pre-exposure regimens. Furthermore, the yellow fever vaccine requires a statutory ten-day waiting period before the official International Certificate of Vaccination becomes legally valid for border crossings. Scheduling your visit early gives us ample time to complete recommended vaccine series and allows your immune system to develop robust biological protection before arrival.

Can I come the week before I fly?

Yes, booking an appointment the week before departure is still very much worth your visit. While certain multi-dose schedules cannot be completed within a single week, partial immunisation often confers meaningful protection, and single-dose vaccines like typhoid can be administered immediately. During a late consultation, our clinicians prioritize essential protections, review travel health precautions, and prescribe medications for altitude illness or self-treatment of travellers' diarrhea. We will always offer practical, effective care regardless of how soon your flight departs.

Do children need a different plan?

Yes, paediatric travellers require carefully tailored travel health plans. Children have unique physical vulnerabilities, differing immune responses, and distinct metabolic dosing requirements. At Tabiji Clinic, nurse Priya Raman RN oversees paediatric consultations, reviewing provincial routine childhood vaccines to ensure primary schedules are up to date before adding destination-specific travel doses. We adapt vaccine schedules to the child's age and weight, while providing parents with practical guidance on insect repellents, sun protection, hydration, and safe food practices abroad.

What if I lose my booklet?

If you misplace your official vaccination booklet, we can re-issue your records. For a fee of CA$40, our records desk reviews clinic archives and verified documentation from previous visits. We transcribe your confirmed immunisation history into a replacement International Certificate of Vaccination booklet, complete with batch numbers, dates, clinician signatures, and official clinic stamps. We also provide an accompanying medical summary letter for your files. This service ensures you carry valid, verified documentation for future border entries and visa requirements.

What should I bring to my consultation?

Please bring your detailed travel itinerary, including dates, transit routes, and accommodation types. Bring any existing physical vaccination records, yellow cards, or childhood health records you possess so we can avoid repeating previously received doses. Additionally, bring a list of all current prescription medications, over-the-counter supplements, and noted medical allergies. Finally, if you are traveling to a region that requires the yellow fever vaccine, bring your current passport number, as this must be recorded directly onto your official certificate.

How do fees and health insurance coverage work?

We confirm your plan and its total before any dose is given. Our consultation fee is CA$95 for an initial sixty-minute visit, follow-up visits are CA$35, and vaccines are priced individually in Canadian dollars. While travel consultations and preventive travel vaccines are not covered by provincial health plans, many extended private health benefits and corporate insurance plans provide partial or complete reimbursement. We supply itemised receipts containing clinician identification and pharmaceutical DIN numbers to facilitate your insurance claim.

pages.title: About the Clinic
pages.content:
About

About the Clinic

Tabiji Clinic is an independent travel health and vaccination practice in Vancouver, preparing travellers for the specific conditions of their destination.

Our clinic

A small clinic for long journeys

Founded in 2014 by Dr. Lena Okoye, Tabiji Clinic was established following her ten years of medical practice in expedition medicine. Working in remote environments made it clear that generic travel advice often misses what travellers actually encounter on the ground. Most people do not need an exhaustive list of every conceivable vaccine. Instead, they require precise guidance tailored to their exact itinerary, the season of travel, and the places where they will sleep. We operate from our clinic on the second floor of 418 Water Street in Vancouver, offering a quiet, clinical setting dedicated entirely to pre-travel care and immunisation.

Meet the team

Why the first visit is a full hour

Every initial consultation at Tabiji Clinic is scheduled for a full sixty minutes. Rushing through travel immunisations leads to missed exposures or unnecessary injections. During the first twenty minutes, we sit together to review your itinerary map, border crossings, elevation profiles, and medical history. The next twenty-five minutes are reserved for administering required vaccines and observing a fifteen-minute rest period in our clinic. The final fifteen minutes are spent documenting every lot number, signing certificates, and explaining follow-up care. An unhurried hour ensures you depart with confidence, clear records, and appropriate protection.

Cold chain integrity and vaccine handling

Vaccines are delicate biological products whose stability depends on uninterrupted temperature control. At Tabiji Clinic, our vaccine inventory and cold chain protocols are managed by our pharmacist, Samuel Achterberg. Biologicals are stored in dedicated medical refrigeration units that continuously monitor and record temperatures within strict clinical parameters. We maintain rigorous documentation for every shipment that enters our dispensary. By protecting the cold chain from delivery through to injection, our Gastown practice protects the quality and storage condition of every vial administered.

pages.title: Contact and Visit
pages.content:
Contact

Contact and Visit

Tabiji Clinic is conveniently located in historic Gastown, just a short walk from Waterfront Station. We welcome your inquiries and look forward to preparing you for your journey.

Getting here

Getting here and neighbourhood access

Tabiji Clinic is located on the second floor at 418 Water Street, Vancouver, BC V6B 1B6, in the heart of historic Gastown. Our clinic is positioned just a four-minute walk from Waterfront Station, providing transit connections via the Expo, Millennium, and Canada Lines, as well as the SeaBus and West Coast Express. For those arriving on foot, our entrance is situated on Water Street between Richards and Cambie Streets. Paid street parking and public parkades are available throughout the immediate neighbourhood.

Clinic hours and appointment scheduling

Our clinic is open Monday through Friday from 9:00 to 18:00, and on Saturday from 9:00 to 13:00. We are closed on Sunday and statutory holidays. We operate primarily by appointment to ensure every patient receives our full sixty-minute consultation. We encourage booking approximately six weeks before departure, though late appointments are always accommodated when schedules permit. You can book an appointment by phoning our front desk directly at 604-555-0142 during opening hours.

Direct communication and enquiries

For general inquiries, scheduling questions, or record requests, you can contact our administrative desk by email at hello@tabiji-clinic.example or by telephone at 604-555-0142. Mei-Lin Chou manages incoming correspondence and will assist you with appointment coordination or document preparation. If you represent an employer, school, or university group planning an expedition of eight or more people, please mention group coordination so we can connect you directly with Tomás Varga.

Bring your itinerary

When you arrive for your visit, please bring your printed or digital itinerary, details of your lodging arrangements, previous vaccination records, and a list of any regular medications. If you require yellow fever vaccination for your route, please remember to bring your passport number so we can issue your official certificate immediately. Our clinicians look forward to welcoming you to our Gastown practice and tailoring an unhurried, evidence-based plan for your upcoming travels.

posts.title: Three Weeks Overland, Nairobi to Kigali
posts.excerpt: A detailed review of a cross-border East African itinerary illustrates why route details and certificate timing matter as much as individual vaccine choices.
posts.content:
When two travellers arrived at Tabiji Clinic planning an overland route from Nairobi to Kigali, they brought a hand-drawn map of their journey. Over three weeks, their plan was to travel westward from Kenya's central highlands into Uganda's Queen Elizabeth National Park, before crossing southward over the land border into northern Rwanda. On a standard country checklist, each of these nations lists multiple recommended travel vaccines. However, when we sat down at our Gastown clinic for our standard sixty-minute consultation, our focus was not on broad regional generalisations, but on the precise transitions where geography, accommodation, and international border regulations intersect.

The foundation of the appointment was an unhurried twenty-minute review of the itinerary led by Dr. Lena Okoye. Tracing the route revealed that while the travellers planned comfortable hotel stays in Nairobi and Kigali, their days in western Uganda would involve rural guesthouses and tented accommodation near freshwater lakes. This distinct exposure shifted our clinical priorities toward food and waterborne protections, specifically single-dose injectable typhoid at CA$95 and the hepatitis A vaccine at CA$90 per dose. By examining where they would sleep and eat rather than simply noting the countries on their tickets, we avoided unnecessary immunisations while securing the defences that matched their genuine day-to-day risk.

The central question of the journey was the yellow fever requirement for cross-border transit. While Kenya does not mandate yellow fever vaccination for entry from North America, overland entry into Rwanda from an endemic transit zone like Uganda requires presentation of a valid International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis. Under World Health Organization standards, this certificate only achieves legal validity ten days after the primary dose is administered. Because the travellers had booked their consultation six weeks before their departure date, we were able to administer the yellow fever vaccine, priced at CA$185 including the certificate, with weeks to spare before their flight. Waiting until the final week before travel would have jeopardised their border crossing at the Rwandan frontier.

Following our discussion, lead nurse Hana Kowalski RN administered the agreed vaccines during the second twenty-five-minute phase of the appointment. This clinical block included our standard fifteen-minute post-injection rest period in our clinic lounge, ensuring that both travellers experienced no immediate adverse reactions. Meanwhile, our administrative desk verified their passport numbers against their official documentation. The final fifteen minutes were dedicated to completing their physical yellow cards, affixing our official clinic stamp, and reviewing insect bite prevention protocols for malaria and viral fevers prevalent in rural river valleys.

An overland journey through East Africa is an extraordinary experience that demands respect for both microbial realities and border logistics. When travellers depart our clinic with verified certificates, appropriate immunity, and practical knowledge, their journey begins on firm footing. Preparation is never about fear; it is about arriving at every border post with calm certainty.
